NJ-2.result: Zack Mullock (D) def. Rep. Jeff Van Drew (R): 50.9% to 48.1% (Ramon Mora Jr., I, 1.0%) with ~98% of expected vote in per NBC; AP figures at 97% tabulated were 137,166 (49.2%) to 130,084 (46.7%). Van Drew conceded election night; AP called it Nov 5. D flip.
NJ-2.pres_2024: Trump +12.5 (270toWin district data); Inquirer: Trump won by nearly 13. No map change (NJ).

explanations.claim: NBC/AP results: Mullock 50.9%, Van Drew 48.1% at ~98% of expected vote; NBC computes a 15.5-point shift toward Democrats vs. the 2024 presidential result.

AP called the race Nov 5 at 4:29 p.m.; Mullock 137,166 (49.2%) to Van Drew 130,084 (46.7%) with 97% tabulated. Van Drew conceded about two hours after polls closed. Electorate ~35% unaffiliated, ~34% R, ~30% D.
Van Drew outspent Mullock: through Oct. 14 Van Drew spent nearly $2.3M vs. just over $855K for Mullock; Van Drew had ~$900K cash left vs. ~$100K.

National analysts rated the seat solid/likely Republican; DCCC added the district to its target list only about a month before the election and did not prioritize it; national help was mostly a last-minute batch of outside spending and surrogate visits (Gov. Sherrill, DNC chair Ken Martin, Rep. Jamie Raskin).

Mullock attacked Van Drew over support for Trump's tariffs and the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and his votes against resolutions to end the Iran war; cost of living, homeownership and flooding were also campaign themes.
Van Drew himself compared the year to the 1974 Watergate midterm: 'it's kind of like a Watergate where it's larger than life and just swept people along with it.'
Voters interviewed cited Van Drew's 2019 party switch and a controversial Vineland data center (which Van Drew said he had no authority over) as reasons to vote against him (voter quotes, not data).

Mullock's campaign credits a field-heavy, all-six-county campaign aimed at unaffiliated voters and a candidate profile as a local mayor ('the Mr. Rogers of Cape May'); Mullock says Republicans crossed over to support him. Van Drew rarely advertised his public schedule.

NJ-2.summary: A local-mayor challenger outspent roughly 3:1 beat a four-term incumbent in a Trump +12.5 seat on a ~15-point swing that no rater anticipated (final ratings: Cook and Inside Likely R, Crystal Ball Lean R, Split Ticket Safe R). The only public poll found (Impact Research, Oct 7-10, D-aligned) had Van Drew up 50-40, outside the 3-week window. Reporting points to the national wave plus local factors (party-switch resentment, data center, Iran war and tariffs); none of it was visible in polling.

PA-1.result: Bob Harvie (D) def. Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R): 52.7% to 47.3% at ~99% of expected vote (NBC). City & State reported 49.1%-44.3% (180,036 to 162,454) at 91% in. AP called it 12:41 a.m. Nov 4. D flip.
PA-1.pres_2024: Harris +0.3 (270toWin district data; City & State describes it as a Harris district). No map change.

explanations.claim: NBC results 52.7-47.3 at 99% expected vote; NBC computes a 5.2-point shift toward Democrats vs. 2024 presidential.
Every precinct in the district shifted toward Harvie, per an Inquirer analysis of voting data; Harvie won most of Lower and Central Bucks and the Montgomery County portion.

DCCC began spending in PA-1 in October, its first investment there since 2020, and said it spent more on broadcast in PA-1 than in the other Pennsylvania swing seats; Gov. Shapiro campaigned in Bucks almost every October weekend.

Fitzpatrick voted with Trump/his party ~70% of the time this term, the least of any House Republican; he voted against the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and Canada tariffs and eventually for ending the Iran war.
Cook moved the race from Lean R to Toss-up days before the election.

Inquirer: Harvie benefited from Trump's 'toxic political brand,' Shapiro's 'lights-out win' and an affordability message; GOP strategist Samuel Chen called it 'clearly a repudiation of the president.'

GOP strategists argued the loss was a product of the wave, not anything Fitzpatrick did; Democratic strategist Anthony Campisi said Trump's low approval made Fitzpatrick's independent brand hard to square. Fitzpatrick's negative ads alleging Harvie was the 'subject' of an FBI investigation (denied by Harvie) did not stop the swing.
Harvie attributes the win to being a countywide-elected commissioner with local roots ('a different kind of candidate... a different time') and four October town halls.

Every county shifted left: Ford won Hamilton County with 55.4% and Delaware with 53.9%; Spartz's margins fell in Howard (37 to ~10.5), Grant (46.8 to 25), Tipton (53 to 32.6) and Madison (26 to 2.8). Turnout was ~260K vs. ~240K in 2022, and turnout appeared weaker in redder areas.

Spartz blamed 'an influx of liberal voters' in Hamilton County, too few rural voters to offset them, Democratic outspending and a 'dishonest campaign.'
IU Indianapolis's Aaron Dusso: 'the blue wave nationally... caught her up'; Ford's single-minded affordability message (drug costs, data centers paying their own utility costs) was 'spot on.'
UIndy's Laura Merrifield Wilson: affordability and dissatisfaction with top-of-ticket Republicans drove the Hamilton County shift.

NV-2.result: Teresa Benitez-Thompson (D) def. David Flippo (R): 50.2% to 44.3% (Independent American Lynn Chapman 5.5%) at ~98% of expected vote (NBC). Open seat (Amodei retired). D flip; first Democrat ever to win the district.
NV-2.pres_2024: Trump +13.9 (270toWin); Nevada Independent: Trump +14. No map change.

explanations.claim: NBC results 50.2-44.3; NBC computes a 20.2-point shift toward Democrats vs. 2024 presidential. The Nevada Independent says all four Nevada districts shifted ~20 points vs. Trump's 2024 margin, and the NV-2 shift vs. 2024 House margins was a little bigger.

Flippo, Trump-endorsed, moved to Reno from a Southern Nevada race and beat Amodei's preferred successor in the primary; he failed to file a personal financial disclosure due in May and faced a report that he exaggerated his military record, plus reports on prior job dismissals.

Benitez-Thompson won Washoe County by ~20 points, carried Carson City (first Democrat in a federal race since Obama 2008), improved Democratic rural-county percentages by double digits and outperformed all statewide Democrats in the district's counties; Flippo underperformed every statewide Republican. Gov. Lombardo (R) got a few thousand more votes than Benitez-Thompson in the district (ticket-splitting), and ~19,000 voters left the race blank.

Record outside spending: Invest in Tomorrow Coalition spent $2M against Flippo; DCCC added her to Red to Blue in October and blanketed Reno TV in late October; the Retail Association of Nevada endorsed a Democrat in NV-2 for the first time. Pop-up PACs promoted IAP candidate Chapman to Republicans, but she performed about as she did in 2024.

A private exit poll of 866 early voters (released post-election by GOP strategist Greg Bailor) showed Benitez-Thompson up 56.8-36.8, with only ~3/4 of Republicans backing Flippo and ~1 in 7 backing her.

Retiring Rep. Amodei: she was 'better qualified... in people's minds' than Flippo; DCCC: 'This race really exemplifies how much candidate quality matters.' Flippo's consultant argued it was simply 'the worst election in the country' for Republicans in decades.

NV-2.summary: A classic candidate-quality upset: a polished former Assembly majority leader against a scandal-plagued, carpetbagging Trump pick in an open Trump +14 seat, with record outside money and a 20-point swing. The Nevada Independent documents ticket-splitting (Lombardo ran ahead of her) and GOP defections. No public polls fell in the final three weeks; the last was GBAO (D) Aug 31-Sep 3 at 38-37. No rater picked her (three Lean R, Inside Tilt R).

MT-1.result: Sam Forstag (D) def. Aaron Flint (R): 50.5% to 46.6% (Libertarian Nick Sheedy 2.9%) per NBC; Montana SoS final tally 132,003 to 122,694. Open seat (Zinke retired). Flint conceded election night; AP called it 10:02 a.m. Nov 5. D flip; first Democrat elected to the U.S. House from western Montana since 1994.

explanations.claim: NBC results 50.5-46.6; NBC computes a 15.8-point shift toward Democrats vs. 2024 presidential.
Missoula County broke 71-27 and Gallatin 61-37 for Forstag in early returns; Flint led on Flathead County votes.

Mid-October, Fox News and Cook moved the race to Toss-up and Inside to Tilt R; Cook cited heavy spending by House Majority PAC and Trump's MAGA Inc. Trump rallied for Flint in Kalispell on Oct 14; former GOP Gov. Marc Racicot campaigned with Forstag.
Forstag, a smokejumper and Forest Service union leader, ran against Forest Service cuts and the One Big Beautiful Bill's Medicaid/SNAP cuts and held 80+ town halls and meet-and-greets.

MSU-Billings pollster Hope Gentry said the district was 'very close and people might be likely to split tickets'; the Mountain State Poll found 55% disapproval of U.S. military action in Iran and 65% opposition to new data centers statewide.

MT-1.summary: An open Trump +11.5 seat flipped on a 16-point swing powered by Missoula and Gallatin, with a union smokejumper running against federal land and health cuts. Every poll in the final three weeks had Forstag ahead or tied, including two Emerson polls and MSU-Billings. Split Ticket and Crystal Ball picked him and Cook and Inside had it Toss-up, so our 46% was a near coin-flip consistent with the data.
MT-1._notes: Final ratings source: Final pre-election ratings as mirrored by 270toWin (Split Ticket map updated Nov 2; Crystal Ball, Cook, Inside Elections updated Nov 3, 2026). 2024 presidential margins are from the 'margin_president' field in 270toWin's district data (current lines). NBC's 'shift' is NBC's own computation vs. the 2024 presidential vote.

MO-2.result: Fred Wellman (D) def. Rep. Ann Wagner (R): 51.1% to 46.2% (Libertarian Brandon Daugherty 2.7%) at ~99% of expected vote (NBC); STLPR/KCUR: 51%-46%. Wagner conceded election night. D flip; first Democrat to win the seat since 1990.
MO-2.pres_2024: Trump +7.9 on the 2022 lines actually used (270toWin); Kyle Kondik: Trump by about 8. Correction to the premise: Missouri did NOT use a new map in 2026. The Trump-backed 2025 map was suspended by a referendum petition (vote on Nov 3), and STLPR/KCUR report the U.S. Supreme Court ruled against using it, so the 2022 lines applied.

explanations.claim: NBC results 51.1-46.2; NBC computes a 12.6-point shift toward Democrats vs. 2024 presidential.
Missouri used its 2022 congressional lines; the GOP's 2025 map, which would have been more favorable to Wagner, was not used (referendum and Supreme Court ruling).
Missouri is using lines approved in 2022 because opponents of the 2025 Trump-backed map gathered enough signatures to force a referendum on Nov 3.
STLPR/KCUR: Wellman's victory 'may be partly attributed' to the 2022 maps being used, and Wagner's loss came amid a backlash over high gas prices, tariffs and the Iran war.

Wellman, a MeidasTouch podcast host with a large anti-Trump online following, had union support and ran on workers' rights, ACA subsidies and requiring congressional approval of military action; Wagner's 2026 ads attacked Wellman heavily, unlike in 2022/2024.
Crystal Ball's Kyle Kondik flagged MO-2 among about six seats that 'could flip if Democrats really kind of blow things out.'

MO-2.summary: Wellman flipped a Trump +8 suburban St. Louis seat by 5 points on a 12.6-point swing. Republicans' more favorable 2025 map was never used, so our premise of 'new maps in Missouri' is wrong for this race. Every poll in the final three weeks had Wellman ahead (Emerson twice, PPP), but no final rating picked him: Silver Bulletin flagged it as the most competitive race and Crystal Ball had moved it to Toss-up in October before ending at Lean R.
MO-2._notes: Silver Bulletin placed MO-2 atop its most-competitive list in late October (STLPR, linking a Wellman campaign Facebook post); Crystal Ball moved it to Toss-up in October (https://centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/2026-rating-changes/) but its final forced-choice rating was Lean R (https://www.270towin.com/2026-house-election/table/crystal-ball-2026-house-forecast). Cook final: Likely R; Inside: Safe R; Split Ticket: Lean R. Final ratings source: Final pre-election ratings as mirrored by 270toWin (Split Ticket map updated Nov 2; Crystal Ball, Cook, Inside Elections updated Nov 3, 2026). 2024 presidential margins are from the 'margin_president' field in 270toWin's district data (current lines). NBC's 'shift' is NBC's own computation vs. the 2024 presidential vote.
